title: A punctured normal root stage is integrally closed after ind-etale base change
statement: Let $B,A$ be commutative rings, with $A$ a $B$-algebra such that $B\to A$ is ind-etale, meaning a filtered colimit of etale $B$-algebras [def-weil-pbc-ind-etale-algebra]. Let $m>0$, $r\geq0$, $t:\operatorname{Fin}(r)\to B$, $f=\prod_i t_i$, and $C=B[x_i]/(x_i^m-t_i)$. Assume multiplication by the image of $f$ on $C$ is injective, and every prime localization of $C$ is an integrally closed domain [def-sfb-parameter-root-algebra, def-weil-pbc-normal-ring]. Put $S=A\otimes_B C$ and $U=S[1/f]$, with the actual pushout presentations and structural map $\iota:S\to U$ [def-sfb-active-root-normalization-pushout-data]. Then $\iota$ is injective and, for every $x\in U$, $x$ is integral over $S$ if and only if $x=\iota(a)$ for some $a\in S$. No characteristic or geometric-point presentation is assumed.

proof.text: Regularity embeds C[1/f] into the total fraction ring of C. Map an integral element through that embedding. Normality and the normal total-fraction theorem put it in C; injectivity puts the original element in C. Thus the integral closure of C in C[1/f] is canonically C.

Write its filtered presentation as $A=\varinjlim_\lambda A_\lambda$, with every $A_\lambda$ finitely presented etale over $B$. The tensor-colimit lemma identifies $S_m=C_m\otimes_B A$ with $\varinjlim_\lambda(C_m\otimes_B A_\lambda)$. By etale base change these terms are etale over $C_m$, and the finite-presentation lemma makes them finitely presented. Thus $C_m\to S_m$ is ind-etale, exactly in the sense needed for integral-closure base change.

Apply the ind-etale integral-closure base-change theorem to C, S and the ambient C[1/f]. The source comparison is S tensor_C C = S. Localization commutes with tensor product by their universal properties, identifying its target ambient ring with U through the structural map. Bijectivity onto the integral-closure subalgebra proves both injectivity of i and the displayed characterization. Structural elements are integral by X-a.
